entries.39a6af8b04c3ff409bf271cdc2ee45a63613077c: <div sID="gen19729" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="4" osisID="Hos.4" sID="Hos.4"/> <div eID="gen19729" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19730" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen19731" type="x-p"/> Prophets were sent to be reprovers, to tell people of their faults, and to warn them of the judgments of God, to which by sin they exposed themselves; so the prophet is employed in this and the following chapters. He is here, as counsel for the King of kings, opening an indictment against the people of Israel, and labouring to convince them of sin, and of their misery and danger because of sin, that he might prevail with them to repent and reform. I. He shows them what were the grounds of God's controversy with them, a general prevalency of vice and profaneness (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.1-Hos.4.2">ver. 1, 2</reference>), ignorance and forgetfulness of God (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.6-Hos.4.7">ver. 6, 7</reference>), the worldly-mindedness of the priests (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.8">ver. 8</reference>), drunkenness and uncleanness (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.11">ver. 11</reference>), using divination and witchcraft (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.12">ver. 12</reference>), offering sacrifice in the high places (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.13">ver. 13</reference>), whoredoms (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.14">ver. 14</reference>, <reference osisRef="Hos.4.18">18</reference>), and bribery among magistrates, <reference osisRef="Hos.4.18">ver. 18</reference>. II. He shows them what would be the consequences of God's controversy. God would punish them for these things, <reference osisRef="Hos.4.9">ver. 9</reference>. The whole land should be laid waste (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.3">ver. 3</reference>), all sorts of people cut off (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.5">ver. 5</reference>), their honour lost (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.7">ver. 7</reference>), their creature-comforts unsatisfying (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.10">ver. 10</reference>), and themselves made ashamed, <reference osisRef="Hos.4.19">ver. 19</reference>. And, which is several times mentioned here as the sorest judgment of all, they should be let alone in their sins (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.17">ver. 17</reference>), they shall not reprove one another (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.4">ver. 4</reference>), God will not punish them (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.14">ver. 14</reference>), nay, he will let them prosper, <reference osisRef="Hos.4.16">ver. 16</reference>. III. He gives warning to Judah not to tread in the steps of Israel, because they saw their steps went down to hell, <reference osisRef="Hos.4.15">ver. 15</reference>.
entries.d23c173810b72127725a82d93eadf9ddff3c56e4: <div eID="gen19731" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen19730" type="introduction"/> <title type="x-s3">The Sinfulness of Israel. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 758.)</title> <div sID="gen19732" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">1</hi> Hear the word of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , ye children of Israel: for the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land. <hi type="super">2</hi> By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood. <hi type="super">3</hi> Therefore shall the land mourn, and every one that dwelleth therein shall languish, with the beasts of the field, and with the fowls of heaven; yea, the fishes of the sea also shall be taken away. <hi type="super">4</hi> Yet let no man strive, nor reprove another: for thy people <hi type="italic">are</hi> as they that strive with the priest. <hi type="super">5</hi> Therefore shalt thou fall in the day, and the prophet also shall fall with thee in the night, and I will destroy thy mother. <div eID="gen19732" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19733" type="x-p"/> Here is, I. The court set, and both attendance and attention demanded: "<hi type="italic">Hear the word of the Lord, you children of Israel,</hi> for to you is the word of this conviction sent, whether you will hear or whether you will forbear." Whom may God expect to give him a fair hearing, and take from him a fair warning, but the children of Israel, his own professing people? Yea, they will be ready enough to hear when God speaks comfortably to them; but are they willing to hear when he has a controversy with them? Yes, they must hear him when he pleads against them, when he has something to lay to their charge: <hi type="italic">The Lord has a controversy with the inhabitants of the land,</hi> of this land, of this holy land. Note, Sin is the great mischief-maker; it sows discord between God and Israel. God sees sin in his own people, and a good action he has against them for it. Some more particular actions lie against his own people, which do not lie against other sinners. He has a controversy with them for breaking covenant with him, for bringing a reproach upon him, and for an ungrateful return to him for his favours. God's controversy will be pleaded, pleaded by the judgments of his mouth before they are pleaded by the judgments of his hand, that he may be justified in all he does and may make it appear that he desires not the death of sinners; and God's pleadings ought to be attended to, for, sooner or later, they shall have a hearing. <div eID="gen19733" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19734" type="x-p"/> II. The indictment read, by which the whole nation stands charged with crimes of a heinous nature, by which God is highly provoked. 1. They are charged with national omissions of the most important duties: <hi type="italic">There is no truth nor mercy,</hi> neither justice nor charity, these most <hi type="italic">weighty matters of the law,</hi> as our Saviour accounts them (<reference osisRef="Matt.23.23">Matt. xxiii. 23</reference>), <hi type="italic">judgment, mercy, and faith.</hi> The generality of the people seemed to have no sense at all of the thing called honesty; they made no conscience of what they said and did, though ever so contrary to the truth and injurious to their neighbour. Much less had they any sense of mercy, or any obligation they were under to pity and help the poor. And it is not strange that there is no truth and mercy when there is <hi type="italic">no knowledge of God in the land.</hi> What good can be expected where there is no knowledge of God? It was the privilege of that land that <hi type="italic">in Israel God was</hi> made <hi type="italic">known,</hi> and his <hi type="italic">name</hi> was <hi type="italic">great,</hi> which was an aggravation of their sin, that they did not <hi type="italic">know him,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ps.76.1">Ps. lxxvi. 1</reference>. 2. Hence follows national commissions of the most enormous sins against both the first and second table, for they had no regard at all to either. <hi type="italic">Swearing,</hi> and <hi type="italic">lying,</hi> and <hi type="italic">killing,</hi> and <hi type="italic">stealing,</hi> and <hi type="italic">committing adultery,</hi> against the third, ninth, sixth, eighth, and seventh commandments, were to be found in all corners of the land, and among all orders and degrees of men among them, <reference osisRef="Hos.4.2">v. 2</reference>. The corruption was universal; what good people there were among them were either lost or hid, or they hid themselves. By these they <hi type="italic">break out,</hi> that is, they transgress all bounds of reason and conscience, and the divine law; <hi type="italic">they have exceeded</hi> (<reference osisRef="Job.36.9">Job xxxvi. 9</reference>); they have been <hi type="italic">overmuch wicked</hi> (<reference osisRef="Eccl.7.17">Eccl. vii. 17</reference>); they suffer their corruptions to break out; they themselves break over, and break through, all that stands in their way and would stop them in their sinful career, as water overflows the banks. Note, Sin is a violent thing and its power exorbitant; when men's hearts are <hi type="italic">fully set in them to do evil</hi> (<reference osisRef="Eccl.8.11">Eccl. viii. 11</reference>) <hi type="italic">what will be restrained from them?</hi> <reference osisRef="Gen.11.6">Gen. xi. 6</reference>. When they break out thus <hi type="italic">blood touches blood,</hi> that is, abundance of murders are committed in all parts of the country, and, as it were, in a constant series and succession. <hi type="italic">Cædes aliæ aliis sunt contiguæ—Murders touch murders;</hi> a stream of blood runs down among them, even royal blood. It was about this time that there was so much blood shed in grasping at the crown; Shallum slew Zechariah, and Menahem slew Shallum, Pekah slew Pekahiah, and Hoshea slew Pekah; and the like bloody work, it is likely, there was among other contenders, so that the land was <hi type="italic">polluted with blood</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ps.106.38">Ps. cvi. 38</reference>); <hi type="italic">it was filled with blood from one end to the other,</hi> <reference osisRef="2Kgs.21.16">2 Kings xxi. 16</reference>. <div eID="gen19734" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19735" type="x-p"/> III. Sentence passed upon this guilty and polluted land, <reference osisRef="Hos.4.3">v. 3</reference>. It shall be utterly destroyed and laid waste. The whole land is infected with sin, and therefore <hi type="italic">the whole land shall mourn</hi> under God's sore judgments, shall sit in mourning, being stripped of all its wealth and beauty. As the valleys are said to <hi type="italic">shout for joy, and sing,</hi> when there are plenty and peace, so here they are said to <hi type="italic">mourn</hi> when by war and famine they are made desolate. The <hi type="italic">whole land shall be brimstone, and salt, and burning,</hi> was as threatened in the law, <reference osisRef="Deut.29.33">Deut. xxix. 33</reference>. They had broken all God's commandments, and now God threatens to take away all their comforts. The <hi type="italic">land mourns</hi> when there is neither <hi type="italic">grass for the cattle nor herbs for the service of man;</hi> and then <hi type="italic">every one that dwells therein shall languish</hi> for want of nice food to support a wasting life, and fret for want of the usual dainties for delight. The <hi type="italic">beasts of the field</hi> will languish, <reference osisRef="Jer.14.5-Jer.14.6">Jer. xiv. 5, 6</reference>. Nay, the destruction of the fruits of the earth shall be so great that there shall not be picking for the <hi type="italic">fowls of the air,</hi> to keep them alive; they shall suffer with man, and their dying, or growing lean, will be a punishment to those who used to have their tables replenished with wild-fowl. Nay, <hi type="italic">the fishes of the sea shall be taken away,</hi> or <hi type="italic">gathered together,</hi> that they may go away in shoals to some other coast, and then the fishing trade will be worth nothing. This desolation shall be in that respect more general than that by Noah's flood, for that did not affect the fishes of the sea, but this shall. It was part of one of the plagues of Egypt that he <hi type="italic">slew their fish</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ps.105.29">Ps. cv. 29</reference>); when the waters are dried the <hi type="italic">fish die,</hi> <reference osisRef="Isa.50.2">Isa. l. 2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zeph.1.2-Zeph.1.3">Zeph. i. 2, 3</reference>. Note, When man becomes disobedient to God, it is just that the inferior creatures should be made unserviceable to man. Oh what reason have we to admire God's patience and mercy to our land, that though there is in it so much swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and adultery, yet there is plenty of flesh, and fish, and fowl, on our tables! <div eID="gen19735" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19736" type="x-p"/> IV. An order of court that no pains should be taken with the condemned criminal to bring him to repentance, with the reason for that order. Observe, 1. The order itself (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.4">v. 4</reference>): <hi type="italic">Yet let no man strive nor reprove another;</hi> let no means be used to reduce and reclaim them; let their physicians give them up as desperate and past cure. It intimates that as long as there is any hope we ought to reprove sinners for their sins; it is a duty we owe to one another to give and to take reproofs; it was one of the laws of Moses (<reference osisRef="Lev.19.17">Lev. xix. 17</reference>), <hi type="italic">Thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour;</hi> it is an instance of brotherly love. Sometimes there is need to rebuke sharply, not only to reprove, but to strive, so loth are men to part with their sins. But it is a sign that persons and people are abandoned to ruin when God says, <hi type="italic">Let them not be reproved.</hi> Yet this is to be understood as God's commands sometimes to the prophets not to <hi type="italic">pray for them,</hi> notwithstanding which they did pray for them; but the meaning is, They are so hardened in sin, and so ripened for ruin, that it will be to little purpose either to deal with them or to deal with God for them. Note, It bodes ill to a people when reprovers are silenced, and when those who should witness against the sins of the times, retire into a corner, and give up the cause. See <reference osisRef="2Chr.25.16">2 Chron. xxv. 16</reference>. 2. The reasons of this order. Let them not reprove one another; for, (1.) They are determined to <hi type="italic">go on in sin,</hi> and no reproofs will cure them of that: <hi type="italic">Thy people are as those that strive with the priests;</hi> they have grown so very impudent in sin, so very insolent, and impatient of reproof, that they will fly in the face even of a priest himself if he should but give them the least check, without any regard to his character and office; and how then can it be thought that they should take a reproof from a private person? Note, Those sinners have their hearts wickedly hardened who quarrel with their ministers for dealing faithfully with them; and those who rebel against ministerial reproof, which is an ordinance of God for their reformation, have forfeited the benefit of brotherly reproof too. Perhaps this may refer to the late wickedness of Joash king of Judah, and his people, who stoned Zechariah, the son of Jehoiada, for delivering them a message from God, <reference osisRef="2Chr.24.21">2 Chron. xxiv. 21</reference>. He was a <hi type="italic">priest;</hi> with him they <hi type="italic">strove</hi> when he was officiating <hi type="italic">between the temple and the altar;</hi> and Dr. Lightfoot thinks the prophet had an eye to his case when he spoke (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.2">v. 2</reference>) of <hi type="italic">blood touching blood;</hi> the blood of the <hi type="italic">sacrificer was mingled with the blood of the sacrifice,</hi> That, says he, was the <hi type="italic">apex</hi> of <hi type="italic">their wickedness</hi>—thence their ruin was to be dated (<reference osisRef="Matt.23.35">Matt. xxiii. 35</reference>), as this is of <hi type="italic">their incorrigibleness,</hi> that they are as those who <hi type="italic">strive with the priest,</hi> therefore let no man reprove them; for, (2.) God also is determined to <hi type="italic">proceed in their ruin</hi> (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.5">v. 5</reference>): "<hi type="italic">Therefore,</hi> because thou wilt take no reproof, no advice, <hi type="italic">thou shalt fall,</hi> and it is in vain for any to think of preventing it, for the <hi type="italic">decree</hi> has <hi type="italic">gone forth.</hi> Thou shalt stumble and <hi type="italic">fall in the day,</hi> and <hi type="italic">the prophet,</hi> the false prophet that flattered and seduced thee, shall <hi type="italic">fall with thee in the night;</hi> both thou and thy prophet shall fall <hi type="italic">night and day,</hi> shall be continually falling into one calamity or other; the darkness of the night shall not help to cover thee from trouble nor the light of the day help thee to flee from it." The prophets are blind leaders and the people blind followers; and to the blind day and night are alike, so that whether it be day or night both shall <hi type="italic">fall together into the ditch.</hi> "Thou shalt fall <hi type="italic">in the day,</hi> when thy fall is least feared by thyself and thou art very <hi type="italic">secure;</hi> and <hi type="italic">in the day,</hi> when it will be seen and observed by others, and turn most to thy shame; and the prophet shall <hi type="italic">fall in the night,</hi> when to himself it will be most terrible." Note, The ruin of those who have helped to ruin others will, in a special manner, be intolerable. And did the children think that when they were in danger of falling their mother would help them? It shall be in vain to expect it, for <hi type="italic">I will destroy thy mother,</hi> Samaria, the mother-city, the whole <hi type="italic">state,</hi> or <hi type="italic">kingdom,</hi> which is as a mother to every part. It shall all be <hi type="italic">made silent.</hi> Note, When all are involved in guilt nothing less can be expected than that all should be involved in ruin.
entries.674c51a80c35676539f7d41892e72f433586d106: <div eID="gen19736" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">Grounds of God's Controversy with Israel; The Sins of the Priests and People. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi>  758.)</title> <div sID="gen19737" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">6</hi> My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children. <hi type="super">7</hi> As they were increased, so they sinned against me: <hi type="italic">therefore</hi> will I change their glory into shame. <hi type="super">8</hi> They eat up the sin of my people, and they set their heart on their iniquity. <hi type="super">9</hi> And there shall be, like people, like priest: and I will punish them for their ways, and reward them their doings. <hi type="super">10</hi> For they shall eat, and not have enough: they shall commit whoredom, and shall not increase: because they have left off to take heed to the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> . <hi type="super">11</hi> Whoredom and wine and new wine take away the heart. <div eID="gen19737" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19738" type="x-p"/> God is here proceeding in his controversy both with the priests and with the people. <hi type="italic">The people</hi> were as those <hi type="italic">that strove with the priests</hi> (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.4">v. 4</reference>) when they had priests that did their duty; but the generality of them lived in the neglect of their duty, and here is a word for those priests, and for the people that love to have it so, <reference osisRef="Jer.5.31">Jer. v. 31</reference>. And it is observable here how the punishment answers to the sin, and how, for the justifying of his own proceedings, God sets the one over-against the other. <div eID="gen19738" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19739" type="x-p"/> I. The people <hi type="italic">strove with the priests</hi> that should have taught them the knowledge of God; justly therefore were they <hi type="italic">destroyed for lack of knowledge,</hi> <reference osisRef="Hos.4.6">v. 6</reference>. Note, Those that rebel against the light can expect no other than to perish in the dark. Or it is a charge upon the priests, who should have been still <hi type="italic">teaching the people knowledge</hi> (<reference osisRef="Eccl.12.9">Eccl. xii. 9</reference>), but they did not, or did it in such a manner that it was as if they had not done it at all, so there was <hi type="italic">no knowledge of God in the land;</hi> and because there was no vision, or none to any purpose, the people <hi type="italic">perished,</hi> <reference osisRef="Prov.29.18">Prov. xxix. 18</reference>. Note, Ignorance is so far from being the mother of devotion that it is the mother of destruction; lack of knowledge is ruining to any person or people. They are <hi type="italic">my people</hi> that are thus <hi type="italic">destroyed;</hi> their relation to God as his people aggravates both their sin in not taking pains to get the knowledge of that God whose command they were under and with whom they were taken into covenant, and likewise the sin of those who should have taught them; God set his children to school to them, and they never minded them nor took any pains with them. <div eID="gen19739" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19740" type="x-p"/> II. Both priests and people rejected knowledge; and justly therefore will God <hi type="italic">reject them.</hi> The reason why the people did not learn, and the priests did not teach, was not because they had not the light, but because they hated it—not because they had not ways of coming to the knowledge of God and of communicating it, but because they had no heart to it; they <hi type="italic">rejected</hi> it. They <hi type="italic">desired not the knowledge of God's ways,</hi> but put it from them, and shut their eyes against the light; and therefore "<hi type="italic">I will also reject thee;</hi> I will refuse to take cognizance of thee and to own thee; you will not know me, but bid me <hi type="italic">depart;</hi> I will therefore say, <hi type="italic">Depart from me, I know you not. Thou</hi> shalt be <hi type="italic">no priest to me.</hi>" 1. The priests shall be no longer admitted to the privileges, or employed in the services, of the priesthood, nor shall they ever be received again, as we find, <reference osisRef="Ezek.44.13">Ezek. xliv. 13</reference>. Note, Ministers that reject knowledge, that are grossly ignorant and scandalous, ought not to be owned as ministers; but that which they <hi type="italic">seem to have</hi> should be <hi type="italic">taken away,</hi> <reference osisRef="Luke.8.18">Luke viii. 18</reference>. 2. The people shall be no longer as they have been, a <hi type="italic">kingdom of priests,</hi> a royal priesthood, <reference osisRef="Exod.19.6">Exod. xix. 6</reference>. God's people, by rejecting knowledge, forfeit their honour and profane their own crown. <div eID="gen19740" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19741" type="x-p"/> III. They <hi type="italic">forgot the law of God,</hi> neither desired nor endeavoured to retain it in mind, nor to transmit the remembrance of it to their posterity, and therefore justly will God <hi type="italic">forget</hi> them and <hi type="italic">their children,</hi> the people's children; they did not educate them, as they ought to have done, in the knowledge of God and their duty to him, and therefore God will disown them, as not in covenant with him. Note, If parents do not teach their children, when they are young, to <hi type="italic">remember their Creator,</hi> they cannot expect that their Creator should remember them. Or it may be meant of the priests' children; they shall not succeed them in the priests' office, but shall be reduced to poverty, as is threatened against Eli's house, <reference osisRef="1Sam.2.20">1 Sam. ii. 20</reference>. <div eID="gen19741" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19742" type="x-p"/> IV. They dishonoured God with that which was their honour, and justly therefore will God strip them of it, <reference osisRef="Hos.4.7">v. 7</reference>. It was their honour that they were increased in number, wealth, power, and dignity. The beginning of their nation was small, but in process of time it <hi type="italic">greatly increased,</hi> and grew very considerable; the family of the priests increased wonderfully. But, <hi type="italic">as they were increased, so they sinned</hi> against God. The more populous the nation grew, the more sin was committed and the more profane they were; their wealth, honour, and power, did but make them the more daring in sin. Therefore, says God, <hi type="italic">will I change their glory into shame.</hi> Are their numbers their glory? God will diminish them and make them few. Is their wealth their glory? God will impoverish them and bring them low; so that they shall themselves be ashamed of that which they gloried in. Their priests shall be made <hi type="italic">contemptible and base,</hi> <reference osisRef="Mal.2.9">Mal. ii. 9</reference>. Note, That which is our honour, if we dishonour God with it, will sooner or later be turned into shame to us: for <hi type="italic">those that despise God shall be lightly esteemed,</hi> <reference osisRef="1Sam.2.30">1 Sam. ii. 30</reference>. <div eID="gen19742" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19743" type="x-p"/> V. The priests ate up the sin of God's people, and therefore <hi type="italic">they shall eat and not have enough.</hi> 1. They abused the maintenance that was allowed to the priests, to the priests of the house of Aaron, by the law of God, and to the mock-priests of the calves by their constitution (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.8">v. 8</reference>): <hi type="italic">They eat up the sin of my people,</hi> that is, their sin-offerings. If it be meant of the priests of the calves, it intimates their seizing that which they had no right to; they usurped the revenues of the priests, though they were no priests. If it be meant of those who were legal priests, it intimates their greediness of the profits and perquisites of their office, when they took no care at all to do the duty of it. They feasted upon their part of the offerings of the Lord, but forgot the work for which they were so well paid. They <hi type="italic">set their heart</hi> upon the people's <hi type="italic">iniquities;</hi> they <hi type="italic">lifted up their soul</hi> to them, that is, they were glad then people did commit iniquity, that they might be obliged to bring an offering to make atonement for it, which they should have their share of; the more sins the more sacrifices, and therefore they cared not how much sin people were guilty of. Instead of warning the people against sin, from the consideration of the sacrifices, which showed them what an offence sin was to God, since it needed such an expiation, they emboldened and encouraged the people to sin, since an atonement might be made at so small an expense. Thus they glutted themselves upon the sins of the people, and helped to keep up that which they should have beaten down. Note, It is a very wicked thing to be well pleased with the sins of others because, in some way or other, they may turn to our advantage. 2. God will therefore deny them his blessing upon their maintenance (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.10">v. 10</reference>): <hi type="italic">They shall eat and not have enough.</hi> Though they have great plenty by the abundance of offerings that are brought in, yet they shall have no satisfaction in it. Either their food shall yield no good nourishment or their greedy appetites shall not be satisfied with it. Note, What is unlawfully gained cannot be comfortably used; no, nor that which is inordinately coveted; it is just that the desires which are insatiable should always be unsatisfied, and that those should never have enough who never know when they have enough. See <reference osisRef="Mic.6.14">Mic. vi. 14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hag.1.6">Hag. i. 6</reference>. <div eID="gen19743" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19744" type="x-p"/> VI. The more they increased the more they sinned (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.7">v. 7</reference>), and therefore though they <hi type="italic">commit whoredom,</hi> though they take the most wicked methods to multiply their people, yet <hi type="italic">they shall not increase.</hi> Though they have many wives and concubines, as Solomon had, yet they shall not have their families built up thereby in a numerous progeny, any more than he had. Note, Those that hope any way to increase by unlawful means will be disappointed. And therefore God will thus blast all their projects <hi type="italic">because they have left off to take heed to the Lord;</hi> time was when they had some regard to God, and to his authority over them and interest in them, but they have <hi type="italic">left it off;</hi> they take no heed to his word nor to his providences; they do not eye him in either. They <hi type="italic">forsake him, so as not to take heed to him;</hi> they have apostatized to such a degree that they have no manner of regard to God, but are perfectly <hi type="italic">without God in the world.</hi> Note, Those that leave off to take heed to the Lord leave off all good, and can expect no other than that all good should leave them. <div eID="gen19744" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19745" type="x-p"/> VII. The people and the priests did harden one another in sin; and therefore justly shall they be sharers in the punishment (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.9">v. 9</reference>): <hi type="italic">There shall be, like people, like priest.</hi> So they were in character; people and priest were both alike ignorant and profane, regardless of God and their duty, and addicted to idolatry: and so they shall be in condition; God will bring judgments upon them, that shall be the destruction both of priest and people; the famine that deprives the people of their meat shall deprive the priests of their <hi type="italic">meat-offerings,</hi> <reference osisRef="Joel.1.9">Joel i. 9</reference>. It is part of the description of a universal desolation that it shall be <hi type="italic">as with the people, so with the priest,</hi> <reference osisRef="Isa.24.2">Isa. xxiv. 2</reference>. God's judgments, when they come with commission, will make no difference. Note, Sharers in sin must expect to be sharers in ruin. Thus God will <hi type="italic">punish them</hi> both <hi type="italic">for their ways,</hi> and <hi type="italic">reward them for their doings.</hi> God will <hi type="italic">cause their doings to return upon them</hi> (so the word is); when a sin is committed the sinner thinks <hi type="italic">it is gone</hi> and he shall hear no more of it, but he shall find it <hi type="italic">called over again,</hi> and made to <hi type="italic">return,</hi> either to his humiliation or to his condemnation. <div eID="gen19745" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19746" type="x-p"/> VIII. They indulged themselves in the delights of sense, to hold up their hearts; but they shall find that they <hi type="italic">take away their hearts</hi> (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.11">v. 11</reference>): <hi type="italic">Whoredom, and wine, and new wine take away the heart.</hi> Some join this with the foregoing words. <hi type="italic">They have forsaken the Lord,</hi> to <hi type="italic">take heed to whoredom, and wine, and new wine.</hi> Or, <hi type="italic">Because</hi> these <hi type="italic">have taken away their heart.</hi> Their sensual pleasures have taken them off from their devotions and drowned all that is good in them. Or we may take it as a distinct sentence, containing a great truth which we see confirmed by every day's experience, that drunkenness and uncleanness are sins which besot and infatuate men, weaken and enfeeble them. They take away both the understanding and the courage.
entries.9c1b037010a80425f490854a7394b4f32e95cc84: <div eID="gen19746" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">The Sins of the Priests and the People; Warning to Judah. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 758.)</title> <div sID="gen19747" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">12</hi> My people ask counsel at their stocks, and their staff declareth unto them: for the spirit of whoredoms hath caused <hi type="italic">them</hi> to err, and they have gone a whoring from under their God. <hi type="super">13</hi> They sacrifice upon the tops of the mountains, and burn incense upon the hills, under oaks and poplars and elms, because the shadow thereof <hi type="italic">is</hi> good: therefore your daughters shall commit whoredom, and your spouses shall commit adultery. <hi type="super">14</hi> I will not punish your daughters when they commit whoredom, nor your spouses when they commit adultery: for themselves are separated with whores, and they sacrifice with harlots: therefore the people <hi type="italic">that</hi> doth not understand shall fall. <hi type="super">15</hi> Though thou, Israel, play the harlot, <hi type="italic">yet</hi> let not Judah offend; and come not ye unto Gilgal, neither go ye up to Beth-aven, nor swear, The <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> liveth. <hi type="super">16</hi> For Israel slideth back as a backsliding heifer: now the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> will feed them as a lamb in a large place. <hi type="super">17</hi> Ephraim <hi type="italic">is</hi> joined to idols: let him alone. <hi type="super">18</hi> Their drink is sour: they have committed whoredom continually: her rulers <hi type="italic">with</hi> shame do love, Give ye. <hi type="super">19</hi> The wind hath bound her up in her wings, and they shall be ashamed because of their sacrifices. <div eID="gen19747" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19748" type="x-p"/> In these verses we have, as before, <div eID="gen19748" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19749" type="x-p"/> I. The sins charged upon the people of Israel, for which God had a controversy with them, and they are, <div eID="gen19749" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19750" type="x-p"/> 1. Spiritual whoredom, or idolatry. They have in them a <hi type="italic">spirit of whoredoms,</hi> a strong inclination to that sin; the bent and bias of their hearts are that way; it is <hi type="italic">their own iniquity;</hi> they are carried out towards it with an unaccountable violence, and this <hi type="italic">causes them to err.</hi> Note, The errors and mistakes of the judgment are commonly owing to the corrupt affections; men <hi type="italic">therefore</hi> have a good opinion of sin, because they have a disposition towards it. And having such erroneous notions of idols, and such passionate motions towards them, no marvel that with such a head and such a heart they have <hi type="italic">gone a whoring from under their God,</hi> <reference osisRef="Hos.4.12">v. 12</reference>. They ought to have been in subjection to him as their head and husband, to have been under his guidance and command, but they revolted from their allegiance, and put themselves under the guidance and protection of false gods. So (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.15">v. 15</reference>) Israel has <hi type="italic">played the harlot;</hi> their conduct in the worship of their idols was like that of a harlot, wanton and impudent. And (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.16">v. 16</reference>), <hi type="italic">Israel slideth back as a backsliding heifer,</hi> as an <hi type="italic">untamed</hi> heifer (so some), or as a <hi type="italic">perverse</hi> or <hi type="italic">refractory</hi> one (so others), as a heifer that is turned loose runs madly about the pasture, or, if put under the yoke (which seems rather to be alluded to here), will draw back instead of going forward, will struggle to get her neck out of the yoke and her feet out of the furrow. Thus unruly, ungovernable, untractable, were the people of Israel. They had begun to draw in the yoke of God's ordinances, but they drew back, as <hi type="italic">children of Belial,</hi> that will not endure the yoke; and when the prophets were sent with the goads of reproof, to put them forward, they <hi type="italic">kicked against the pricks,</hi> and ran backwards. The sum of all is (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.17">v. 17</reference>), <hi type="italic">Ephraim is joined to idols,</hi> is perfectly wedded to them; his affections are glued to them, and his heart is upon them. There are two instances given of their spiritual whoredom, in both which they gave that honour to their idols which is due to God only:—(1.) They consulted them as oracles, and used those arts of divination which they had learned from their idolatrous priests (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.12">v. 12</reference>): <hi type="italic">My people ask counsel at their stocks,</hi> their wooden gods; they apply to them for advice and direction in what they should do and for information concerning the event. They <hi type="italic">say to a stock, Thou art my father</hi> (<reference osisRef="Jer.2.27">Jer. ii. 27</reference>); and, if it were indeed a father, it were worthy of this honour; but it was a great affront to God, who was indeed their Father, and whose lively oracles they had among them, with which they had liberty to consult at any time, thus to <hi type="italic">ask counsel at their stocks.</hi> And they expect that their <hi type="italic">staff</hi> should <hi type="italic">declare to them</hi> what course they should take and what the event should be. It is probable that this refers to some wicked methods of divination used among the Gentiles, and which the Jews learned from them, by a <hi type="italic">piece of wood,</hi> or by <hi type="italic">a staff,</hi> like Nebuchadnezzar's divining by <hi type="italic">his arrows,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ezek.21.21">Ezek. xxi. 21</reference>. Note, Those who forsake the oracles of God, to take their measures from the world and the flesh, do in effect but consult with their stocks and their staves. (2.) They offered sacrifice to them as gods, whose favour they wanted and whose wrath they dreaded and deprecated (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.13">v. 13</reference>): <hi type="italic">They sacrifice to them,</hi> to atone and pacify them, and <hi type="italic">burn incense</hi> to them, to please and gratify them, and hope by both to recommend themselves to them. God had pitched upon the place where he would record his name; but they, having forsaken that, chose places for their irreligious rites which pleased their own fancies; they chose, [1.] High places, <hi type="italic">upon the tops of the mountains</hi> and <hi type="italic">upon the hills,</hi> foolishly imagining that the height of the ground gave them some advantage in their approaches towards heaven. [2.] Shady places, <hi type="italic">under oaks, and poplars, and elms, because the shadow thereof</hi> is pleasant to them, especially in those hot countries, and therefore they thought it was pleasing to their gods; or they fancied that a thick shade befriends contemplation, possesses the mind with something of awe, and therefore is proper for devotion. <div eID="gen19750" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19751" type="x-p"/> 2. Corporal whoredom is another crime here charged upon them: <hi type="italic">They have committed whoredom continually,</hi> <reference osisRef="Hos.4.18">v. 18</reference>. They drove a trade of uncleanness; it was not a single act now and then, but their constant practice, as it is of many that have <hi type="italic">eyes full of adultery</hi> and <hi type="italic">which cannot cease from</hi> that <hi type="italic">sin,</hi> <reference osisRef="2Pet.2.14">2 Pet. ii. 14</reference>. Now the abominable filthiness and lewdness that was found in Israel is here spoken of, (1.) As a concomitant of their idolatry; their false gods drew them to it; for the devil whom they worshipped, though a spirit, is an unclean spirit. Those that worshipped idols were <hi type="italic">separated with harlots,</hi> and they <hi type="italic">sacrificed with harlots;</hi> for because they <hi type="italic">liked not to retain God in their knowledge,</hi> but dishonoured him, therefore God <hi type="italic">gave them up to vile affections,</hi> by the indulging of which they <hi type="italic">dishonoured themselves,</hi> <reference osisRef="Rom.1.24">Rom. i. 24</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rom.1.28">28</reference>. (2.) As a punishment of it. The <hi type="italic">men</hi> that worshipped idols were <hi type="italic">separated with harlots</hi> that attended the idolatrous rites, as in the worship of <hi type="italic">Baal-peor,</hi> <reference osisRef="Num.25.1-Num.25.2">Num. xxv. 1, 2</reference>. To punish them for that God gave up their wives and daughters to the like vile affections: They <hi type="italic">committed whoredom and adultery</hi> (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.13">v. 13</reference>), which could not but be a great grief and reproach to their husbands and parents; for those that are not chaste themselves desire to have their wives and daughters so. But thus they might read their sin in their punishment, as David's adultery was punished in the debauching of his concubines by his own son, <reference osisRef="2Sam.12.11">2 Sam. xii. 11</reference>. Note, When the same sin in others is made men's grief and affliction which they have themselves been guilty of they must own that the Lord is righteous. <div eID="gen19751" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19752" type="x-p"/> 3. The perverting of justice, <reference osisRef="Hos.4.18">v. 18</reference>. <hi type="italic">Their rulers</hi> (be it spoken to their shame) <hi type="italic">do love, Give ye,</hi> that is, they love bribes, and have it continually in their mouths, <hi type="italic">Give, give.</hi> They are given to <hi type="italic">filthy lucre;</hi> every one that has any business with them must expect to be asked, What will you give? Though, as rulers, they are bound by office to do justice, yet none can have justice done them without a fee; and you may be sure that for a fee they will do injustice. Note, The love of money is the ruin of equity and the root of all iniquity. But of all men it is a shame for rulers (who should be men <hi type="italic">fearing God</hi> and <hi type="italic">hating covetousness</hi>) to love <hi type="italic">Give ye.</hi> Perhaps this is intended in that part of the charge here, <hi type="italic">Their drink is sour;</hi> it is <hi type="italic">dead;</hi> it is <hi type="italic">gone.</hi> Justice, duly administered, is refreshing, like drink to the thirsty, but when it is perverted, and rulers take rewards either to acquit the guilty or to condemn the innocent, the <hi type="italic">drink is sour;</hi> they <hi type="italic">turn judgment into wormwood,</hi> <reference osisRef="Amos.5.7">Amos v. 7</reference>. Or it may refer in general to the depraved morals of the whole nation; they had lost all their life and spirit, and were as offensive to God as dead and sour drink is to us. See <reference osisRef="Deut.31.32-Deut.31.33">Deut. xxxi. 32, 33</reference>. <div eID="gen19752" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19753" type="x-p"/> II. The tokens of God's wrath against them for their sins. 1. Their wives and daughters should not be punished for the injury and disgrace they did to their families (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.14">v. 14</reference>): <hi type="italic">I will not punish your daughters;</hi> and, not being punished for their sin, they would go on in it. Note, The impunity of one sinner is sometimes made the punishment of another. Or, "<hi type="italic">I will not punish</hi> them as I will punish you; for you must own, as Judah did concerning his daughter-in-law, that <hi type="italic">they are more righteous than you,</hi>" <reference osisRef="Gen.38.26">Gen. xxxviii. 26</reference>. 2. They themselves should prosper for a while, but their prosperity should help to destroy them. It comes in as a token of God's wrath (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.16">v. 16</reference>): <hi type="italic">The Lord will feed them as a lamb in a large place;</hi> they shall have a fat pasture, and a large one, in which they shall be fed to the full, and fed of the best, but it shall be only to prepare them for the slaughter, as a lamb is that is so fed. If they <hi type="italic">wax fat and kick,</hi> they do but wax fat for the butcher. But others make them feed as <hi type="italic">a lamb on the common,</hi> a large place indeed, but where it has short grass and lies exposed. The Shepherd of Israel will turn them both out of his pastures and out of his protection. 3. No means should be used to bring them to repentance (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.17">v. 17</reference>): "<hi type="italic">Ephraim is joined to idols,</hi> is in love with them and addicted to them, and therefore <hi type="italic">let him alone,</hi> as <reference osisRef="Hos.4.4">v. 4</reference>, <hi type="italic">Let no man reprove</hi> him. Let him be given up to <hi type="italic">his own heart's lusts,</hi> and walk <hi type="italic">in his own counsel;</hi> we <hi type="italic">would have healed</hi> him, and he <hi type="italic">would not be healed,</hi> therefore <hi type="italic">forsake</hi> him," See <hi type="italic">what their end will be,</hi> <reference osisRef="Deut.32.20">Deut. xxxii. 20</reference>. Note, It is a sad and sore judgment for any man to be let alone in sin, for God to say concerning a sinner, "He is joined to his idols, the world and the flesh; he is incurably proud, covetous, or profane, an incurable drunkard or adulterer; <hi type="italic">let him alone;</hi> conscience, let him alone; minister, let him alone; providences, let him alone. Let nothing awaken him till the flames of hell do it." The father corrects not the rebellious son any more when he determines to disinherit him. "Those that are not disturbed in their sin will be destroyed for their sin." 4. They should be hurried away with a swift and shameful destruction (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.19">v. 19</reference>): <hi type="italic">The wind has bound her up in her wings,</hi> to carry her away into captivity, suddenly, violently, and irresistibly; he shall take <hi type="italic">them away as with a whirlwind,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ps.58.9">Ps. lviii. 9</reference>. And then <hi type="italic">they shall be ashamed because of their sacrifices,</hi> ashamed of their sin in offering sacrifice to idols, ashamed of their folly in putting themselves to such an expense upon gods that have no power to help them, and thereby making that God their enemy who has almighty power to destroy them. Note, There are sacrifices that men will one day be ashamed of. Those that have sacrificed their time, strength, honour, and all their comforts, to the world and the flesh, will shortly be ashamed of it. Yea, and those that bring to God blind, and lame, and heartless sacrifices, will be ashamed of them too. <div eID="gen19753" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19754" type="x-p"/> III. The warning given to Judah not to sin after the similitude of Israel's transgression. It is said in the close of <reference osisRef="Hos.4.14">v. 14</reference>, <hi type="italic">Those that do not understand shall fall;</hi> those must needs fall that do not understand how to avoid, or get over, the stumbling-blocks they meet with (and therefore <hi type="italic">let him that thinks he stands take heed lest he fall</hi>), particularly the two tribes (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.15">v. 15</reference>): <hi type="italic">Though thou, Israel, play the harlot, yet let not Judah offend.</hi> Though Israel be given to idolatry, yet let not Judah take the infection. Now, 1. This was a very needful caution. The men of Israel were brethren, and near neighbours, to the men of Judah; Israel was more numerous, and at this time in a prosperous condition, and therefore there was danger lest the men of Judah should learn their way and get a snare to their souls. Note, The nearer we are to the infection of sin the more need we have to stand upon our guard. 2. It was a very rational caution: "<hi type="italic">Let Israel play the harlot,</hi> yet let not Judah do so; for Judah has greater means of knowledge than Israel, has the temple and priesthood, and a king of the house of David; from Judah Shiloh is to come; and for Judah God has reserved great blessings in store; therefore <hi type="italic">let not Judah offend,</hi> for more is expected from them than from Israel, they will have more to answer for if they do offend, and from them God will take it more unkindly. If <hi type="italic">Israel play the harlot,</hi> let not Judah do so too, for then God will have no professing people in the world." God bespeaks Judah here, as Christ does the twelve, when many turned their backs upon him, <hi type="italic">Will you also go away?</hi> <reference osisRef="John.6.67">John vi. 67</reference>. Note, Those that have hitherto kept their integrity should, for that reason, still hold it fast, even in times of general apostasy. Now, to preserve Judah from offending as Israel had done, two rules are here given:—(1.) That they might not be guilty of idolatry they must keep at a distance from the places of idolatry: <hi type="italic">Come not you unto Gilgal,</hi> where <hi type="italic">all their wickedness was</hi> (<reference osisRef="Hos.9.15">ch. ix. 15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.12.11">xii. 11</reference>); there they <hi type="italic">multiplied transgression</hi> (<reference osisRef="Amos.4.4">Amos iv. 4</reference>); and perhaps they contracted a veneration for that place because there it was said to Joshua, The place <hi type="italic">where thou standest is holy ground</hi> (<reference osisRef="Josh.5.15">Josh. v. 15</reference>); therefore they are forbidden to <hi type="italic">enter into Gilgal,</hi> <reference osisRef="Amos.5.5">Amos v. 5</reference>. And for the same reason they must <hi type="italic">not go up to Bethel,</hi> here called the <hi type="italic">house of vanity,</hi> for so <hi type="italic">Bethaven</hi> signifies, not the <hi type="italic">house of God,</hi> as <hi type="italic">Bethel</hi> signifies. Note, Those that would be kept from sin, and not fall into the devil's hands, must studiously avoid the occasions of sin and not come upon the devil's ground. (2.) That they might not be guilty of idolatry they must take heed of profaneness, and <hi type="italic">not swear, The Lord liveth.</hi> They are commanded to swear, <hi type="italic">The Lord liveth in truth and righteousness</hi> (<reference osisRef="Jer.4.2">Jer. iv. 2</reference>); and therefore that which is here forbidden is swearing so in untruth and unrighteousness, swearing rashly and lightly, or falsely and with deceit, or swearing by the Lord and the idol, <reference osisRef="Zeph.1.5">Zeph. i. 5</reference>. Note, Those that would be steady in their adherence to God must possess themselves with an awe and reverence of God, and always speak of him with solemnity and seriousness; for those that can make a jest of the true God will make a god of any thing.  <chapter eID="Hos.4"/> <div eID="gen19754" type="x-p"/>

entries.5838cab93e639c0f53393e941b8e557666d6149c: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12277"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 4</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Hos.4.1-Hos.4.19">Ho 4:1-19</reference>. Henceforth the Prophet Speaks Plainly and without Symbol, in Terse, Sententious Propositions.</title> <div sID="gen22359" type="x-p"/> In this chapter he reproves the people and priests for their sins in the interregnum which followed Jeroboam's death; hence there is no mention of the king or his family; and in <reference osisRef="Hos.4.2">Ho 4:2</reference> bloodshed and other evils usual in a civil war are specified.<div eID="gen22359" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22360" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12277"/><hi type="bold">1. Israel--</hi>the ten tribes.<div eID="gen22360" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22361" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">controversy--</hi>judicial ground of complaint (<reference osisRef="Isa.1.18">Is 1:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.25.31">Jr 25:31</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.6.2">Mi 6:2</reference>).<div eID="gen22361" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22362" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">no ... knowledge of God--</hi>exhibited in practice (<reference osisRef="Jer.22.16">Jr 22:16</reference>). <div eID="gen22362" type="x-p"/>
entries.158ea0c4e134bb5257c5781fc675578e9bb541f8: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12278"/><div sID="gen22363" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12278"/><hi type="bold">2. they break out--</hi>bursting through every restraint.<div eID="gen22363" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22364" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">blood toucheth blood--</hi>literally, "bloods." One act of bloodshed follows another without any interval between (see 2Ki 15:8-16, 25; <reference osisRef="Mic.7.2">Mi 7:2</reference>). <div eID="gen22364" type="x-p"/>
entries.f9aee9d6bc21a88eac9b1b404f179a6ea4213b18: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12279"/><div sID="gen22365" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12279"/><hi type="bold">3. land ... languish--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.19.8">Is 19:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.24.4">24:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Joel.1.10">Joe 1:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.12">12</reference>).<div eID="gen22365" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22366" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sea--</hi>including all bodies of water, as pools and even rivers (see on <reference osisRef="Isa.19.5">Is 19:5</reference>). A general drought, the greatest calamity in the East, is threatened. <div eID="gen22366" type="x-p"/>
entries.43e2fc0905542c4be438f7e19b331f8bc574ed80: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12280"/><div sID="gen22367" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12280"/><hi type="bold">4. let no man ... reprove--</hi>Great as is the sin of Israel, it is hopeless to reprove them; for their presumptuous guilt is as great as that of one who refuses to obey the priest when giving judgment in the name of Jehovah, and who therefore is to be put to death (<reference osisRef="Deut.17.12">De 17:12</reference>). They rush on to their own destruction as wilfully as such a one.<div eID="gen22367" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22368" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">thy people--</hi>the ten tribes of Israel; distinct from Judah (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.1">Ho 4:1</reference>). <div eID="gen22368" type="x-p"/>
entries.4d986b72ed280682780c8c7406cde97b1e70a6f4: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12281"/><div sID="gen22369" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12281"/><hi type="bold">5. fall in the day--</hi>in broad daylight, a time when an attack would not be expected (see on <reference osisRef="Jer.6.4">Jr 6:4</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.6.5">5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.15.8">Jr 15:8</reference>).<div eID="gen22369" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22370" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in ... night--</hi>No time, night or day, shall be free from the slaughter of individuals of the people, as well as of the false prophets.<div eID="gen22370" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22371" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">thy mother--</hi>the Israelitish state, of which the citizens are the children (<reference osisRef="Hos.2.2">Ho 2:2</reference>). <div eID="gen22371" type="x-p"/>
entries.b1461fed0ba72a24db5b9d3029dc7cac7af402d6: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12282"/><div sID="gen22372" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12282"/><hi type="bold">6. lack of knowledge--</hi>"of God" (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.1">Ho 4:1</reference>), that is, lack of piety. Their ignorance was wilful, as the epithet, "My people," implies; they ought to have known, having the opportunity, as the people of God.<div eID="gen22372" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22373" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">thou--</hi>O priest, so-called. Not regularly constituted, but still bearing the name, while confounding the worship of Jehovah and of the calves in Beth-el (<reference osisRef="1Kgs.12.29">1Ki 12:29</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Kgs.12.31">31</reference>).<div eID="gen22373" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22374" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">I will ... forget thy children--</hi>Not only those who then were alive should be deprived of the priesthood, but their children who, in the ordinary course would have succeeded them, should be set aside. <div eID="gen22374" type="x-p"/>
entries.0b9b8baec39854f44aeb0ffb58abb9b2a0398437: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12283"/><div sID="gen22375" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12283"/><hi type="bold">7. As they were increased--</hi>in numbers and power. Compare <reference osisRef="Hos.4.6">Ho 4:6</reference>, "thy children," to which their "increase" in numbers refers.<div eID="gen22375" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22376" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">so they sinned--</hi>(Compare <reference osisRef="Hos.10.1">Ho 10:1</reference> and <reference osisRef="Hos.13.6">Ho 13:6</reference>).<div eID="gen22376" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22377" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">will I change their glory into shame--</hi>that is, I will strip them of all they now glory in (their numbers and power), and give them shame instead. A just retribution: as they changed their glory into shame, by idolatry (<reference osisRef="Ps.106.20">Psa 106:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.2.11">Jr 2:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.1.23">Ro 1:23</reference>; <reference osisRef="Phil.3.19">Php 3:19</reference>). <div eID="gen22377" type="x-p"/>
entries.bee3c463fcc3094f271c9f9f40ef3bef234e0bb0: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12284"/><div sID="gen22378" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12284"/><hi type="bold">8. eat ... sin of my people--</hi>that is, the sin offerings (<reference osisRef="Lev.6.26">Le 6:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lev.10.17">10:17</reference>). The priests greedily devoured them.<div eID="gen22378" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22379" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">set their heart on their iniquity--</hi>literally, "lift up the animal soul to lust after," or strongly desire. Compare <reference osisRef="Deut.24.15">De 24:15</reference>, Margin; <reference osisRef="Ps.24.4">Psa 24:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.22.27">Jr 22:27</reference>. The priests set their own hearts on the iniquity of the people, instead of trying to suppress it. For the more the people sinned, the more sacrificial victims in atonement for sin the priests gained. <div eID="gen22379" type="x-p"/>
entries.2651956792a51afb7439d2371c23a5b714346045: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12285"/><div sID="gen22380" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12285"/><hi type="bold">9. like people, like priest--</hi>They are one in guilt; therefore they shall be one in punishment (<reference osisRef="Isa.24.2">Is 24:2</reference>).<div eID="gen22380" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22381" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">reward them their doings--</hi>in homely phrase, "pay them back in their own coin" (<reference osisRef="Prov.1.31">Pr 1:31</reference>). <div eID="gen22381" type="x-p"/>
entries.a53ff25f5c1406e0dda3b11875c46f1b5e61ea2a: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12286"/><div sID="gen22382" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12286"/><hi type="bold">10. eat, and not have enough--</hi>just retribution on those who "eat up (greedily) the sin of My people" (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.8">Ho 4:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.6.14">Mi 6:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hag.1.6">Hag 1:6</reference>).<div eID="gen22382" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22383" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">whoredom, and ... not increase--</hi>literally, "break forth"; used of giving birth to children (<reference osisRef="Gen.28.14">Ge 28:14</reference>, Margin; compare <reference osisRef="Gen.38.29">Ge 38:29</reference>). Not only their wives, but their concubines, shall be barren. To be childless was considered a great calamity among the Jews. <div eID="gen22383" type="x-p"/>
entries.40671a0b00dde6af7bb04b33646bf8078397bc0a: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12287"/><div sID="gen22384" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12287"/>11. A moral truth applicable to all times. The special reference here is to the licentious orgies connected with the Syrian worship, which lured Israel away from the pure worship of God (<reference osisRef="Isa.28.1">Is 28:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.28.7">7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.4.1">Am 4:1</reference>).<div eID="gen22384" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22385" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">take away the heart--</hi>that is, the understanding; make men blind to their own true good (<reference osisRef="Eccl.7.7">Ec 7:7</reference>). <div eID="gen22385" type="x-p"/>
entries.cbc8a2b50a0810fb277c96024f2533f550913ed1: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12288"/><div sID="gen22386" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12288"/>12. Instances of their understanding ("heart") being "taken away."<div eID="gen22386" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22387" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">stocks--</hi>wooden idols (<reference osisRef="Jer.2.27">Jr 2:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hab.2.19">Ha 2:19</reference>).<div eID="gen22387" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22388" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">staff--</hi>alluding to divination by rods (see on <reference osisRef="Ezek.21.21">Eze 21:21</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.21.22">22</reference>). The diviner, says Rosenmuller, threw a rod from him, which was stripped of its bark on one side, not on the other: if the bare side turned uppermost, it was a good omen; if the side with the bark, it was a bad omen. The Arabs used two rods, the one marked God bids, the other, God forbids; whichever came out first, in drawing them out of a case, gave the omen for, or against, an undertaking.<div eID="gen22388" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22389" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">declareth--</hi>that is, is consulted to inform them of future events.<div eID="gen22389" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22390" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">spirit of whoredoms--</hi>a general disposition on the part of all towards idolatry (<reference osisRef="Hos.5.4">Ho 5:4</reference>).<div eID="gen22390" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22391" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">err--</hi>go astray from the true God.<div eID="gen22391" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22392" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">from under their God--</hi>They have gone away from God under whom they were, as a wife is under the dominion of her husband. <div eID="gen22392" type="x-p"/>
entries.fddc80ad137a536a6064027aac673407812e1c7d: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12289"/><div sID="gen22393" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12289"/><hi type="bold">13. upon ... mountains--</hi>High places were selected by idolaters on which to sacrifice, because of their greater nearness to the heavenly hosts which they worshipped (<reference osisRef="Deut.12.2">De 12:2</reference>).<div eID="gen22393" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22394" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">elms--</hi>rather, "terebinths" [Maurer].<div eID="gen22394" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22395" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shadow ... good--</hi>screening the lascivious worshippers from the heat of the sun.<div eID="gen22395" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22396" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">daughters ... commit whoredom ... spouses ... adultery--</hi>in the polluted worship of Astarte, the Phoenician goddess of love. <div eID="gen22396" type="x-p"/>
entries.83acaddc6c2ee5c20c548b0ce3747d3277c2a7c7: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12290"/><div sID="gen22397" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12290"/><hi type="bold">14. I will not punish ... daughters--</hi>I will visit with the heaviest punishments "not" the unchaste "daughters and spouses," but the fathers and husbands; for it is these who "themselves" have set the bad example, so that as compared with the punishment of the latter, that of the former shall seem as nothing [Munster].<div eID="gen22397" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22398" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">separated with whores--</hi>withdrawn from the assembly of worshippers to some receptacle of impurity for carnal connection with whores.<div eID="gen22398" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22399" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sacrifice with harlots--</hi>They commit lewdness with women who devote their persons to be violated in honor of Astarte. (So the Hebrew for "harlots" means, as distinguished from "whores"). Compare <reference osisRef="Num.25.1-Num.25.3">Nu 25:1-3</reference>; and the prohibition, <reference osisRef="Deut.23.18">De 23:18</reference>.<div eID="gen22399" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22400" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">not understand--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.44.18">Is 44:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.45.20">45:20</reference>).<div eID="gen22400" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22401" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shall fall--</hi>shall be cast down. <div eID="gen22401" type="x-p"/>
entries.d0fabf5878ffc40189f0cbf92baf768991daa64b: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12291"/><div sID="gen22402" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12291"/>15. Though Israel's ten tribes indulge in spiritual harlotry, at least thou, Judah, who hast the legal priesthood, and the temple rites, and Jerusalem, do not follow her bad example.<div eID="gen22402" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22403" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Gilgal--</hi>situated between Jordan and Jericho on the confines of Samaria; once a holy place to Jehovah (<reference osisRef="Josh.5.10-Josh.5.15">Jos 5:10-15</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Sam.10.8">1Sa 10:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Sam.15.21">15:21</reference>); afterwards desecrated by idol-worship (<reference osisRef="Hos.9.15">Ho 9:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.12.11">12:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.4.4">Am 4:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.5.5">5:5</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Judg.3.19">Jud 3:19</reference>, Margin).<div eID="gen22403" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22404" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Beth-aven--</hi>that is, "house of vanity" or idols: a name substituted in contempt for Beth-el, "the house of God"; once sacred to Jehovah (<reference osisRef="Gen.28.17">Ge 28:17</reference>, <reference osisRef="Gen.28.19">19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gen.35.7">35:7</reference>), but made by Jeroboam the seat of the worship of the calves (1Ki 12:28-33; 13:1; <reference osisRef="Jer.48.13">Jr 48:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.3.14">Am 3:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.7.13">7:13</reference>). "Go up" refers to the fact that Beth-el was on a hill (<reference osisRef="Josh.16.1">Jos 16:1</reference>).<div eID="gen22404" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22405" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">nor swear, The Lord liveth--</hi>This formula of oath was appointed by God Himself (<reference osisRef="Deut.6.13">De 6:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.10.20">10:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.4.2">Jr 4:2</reference>). It is therefore here forbidden not absolutely, but in conjunction with idolatry and falsehood (<reference osisRef="Isa.48.1">Is 48:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.20.39">Eze 20:39</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zeph.1.5">Zep 1:5</reference>). <div eID="gen22405" type="x-p"/>
entries.c908979f470c51ab039c0653e458ee4f9881b13e: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12292"/><div sID="gen22406" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12292"/><hi type="bold">16. backsliding--</hi>Translate, "Israel is refractory, as a refractory heifer," namely, one that throws the yoke off her neck. Israel had represented God under the form of "calves" (<reference osisRef="1Kgs.12.28">1Ki 12:28</reference>); but it is she herself who is one.<div eID="gen22406" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22407" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">lamb in a large place--</hi>not in a good sense, as in <reference osisRef="Isa.30.23">Is 30:23</reference>. Here there is irony: lambs like a large pasture; but it is not so safe for them as a small one, duly fenced from wild beasts. God will "feed" them, but it shall be with the "rod" (<reference osisRef="Mic.7.14">Mi 7:14</reference>). It shall be no longer in the narrow territory of Israel, but "in a large place," namely, they shall be scattered in exile over the wide realm of Assyria, a prey to their foes; as lambs, which are timid, gregarious, and not solitary, are a prey when scattered asunder to wild beasts. <div eID="gen22407" type="x-p"/>
entries.b7bf61b8582e57da929a5c87feef353c0721b1a2: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12293"/><div sID="gen22408" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12293"/><hi type="bold">17. Ephraim--</hi>the ten tribes. Judah was at this time not so given to idolatry as afterwards.<div eID="gen22408" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22409" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">joined to--</hi>closely and voluntarily; identifying themselves with them as a whoremonger becomes one flesh with the harlot (<reference osisRef="Num.25.3">Nu 25:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.6.16">1Co 6:16</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.6.17">17</reference>).<div eID="gen22409" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22410" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">idols--</hi>The Hebrew means also "sorrows," "pains," implying the pain which idolatry brings on its votaries.<div eID="gen22410" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22411" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">let him alone--</hi>Leave him to himself. Let him reap the fruits of his own perverse choice; his case is desperate; say nothing to him (compare <reference osisRef="Jer.7.16">Jr 7:16</reference>). Here <reference osisRef="Hos.4.15">Ho 4:15</reference> shows the address is to Judah, to avoid the contagion of Israel's bad example. He is bent on his own ruin; leave him to his fate, lest, instead of saving him, thou fall thyself (<reference osisRef="Isa.48.20">Is 48:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.50.8">Jr 50:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.51.6">51:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.51.45">45</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Cor.6.17">2Co 6:17</reference>). <div eID="gen22411" type="x-p"/>
entries.ec2f43c1033bd311f77f488a2bc9a47288902590: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12294"/><div sID="gen22412" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12294"/><hi type="bold">18. Their drink is sour--</hi>metaphor for utter degeneracy of principle (<reference osisRef="Isa.1.22">Is 1:22</reference>). Or, unbridled licentiousness; not mere ordinary sin, but as abandoned as drunkards who vomit and smell sour with wine potations [Calvin]. Maurer not so well translates, "When their drinking is over, they commit whoredoms," namely, in honor of Astarte (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.13">Ho 4:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Hos.4.14">14</reference>).<div eID="gen22412" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22413" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">her rulers--</hi>Israel's; literally, "shields" (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.47.9">Psa 47:9</reference>).<div eID="gen22413" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22414" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">with shame ... love, Give ye--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Prov.30.15">Pr 30:15</reference>). No remedy could be effectual against their corruptions since the very rulers sold justice for gifts [Calvin]. Maurer translates, "The rulers are marvelously enamored of shame." English Version is better. <div eID="gen22414" type="x-p"/>
entries.72d87a2a1a240ad772c7fa473c25ec772105281f: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12295"/><div sID="gen22415" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12295"/>19. Israel shall be swept away from her land (<reference osisRef="Hos.4.16">Ho 4:16</reference>) suddenly and violently as if by "the wings of the wind" (<reference osisRef="Ps.18.10">Psa 18:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.104.3">104:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.4.11">Jr 4:11</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.4.12">12</reference>).<div eID="gen22415" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22416" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">ashamed ... of their sacrifices--</hi>disappointed to their shame in their hope of help through their sacrifices to idols. <chapter eID="Hos.4"/>

entries.cac5c5b8d936b9d02b9cfa0d7cc50e3e9d84b7e1: <div eID="gen33613" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen33614" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen33615" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen33615" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen33614" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen33616" type="x-p"/> The prophet charges his people with their enormous sins, <reference osisRef="Hos.4.1">Hos 4:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Hos.4.2">Hos 4:2</reference>; in consequence of which they are threatened with heavy judgments, <reference osisRef="Hos.4.3-Hos.4.5">Hos 4:3-5</reference>. God himself is then introduced complaining of the ignorance and obstinacy of Israel; and as their priests had a large share in the common guilt, it is declared that they shall be visited with a proportionable share of the common ruin, <reference osisRef="Hos.4.6-Hos.4.11">Hos 4:6-11</reference>. The sins of idolatry and divination are then particularly reproved, <reference osisRef="Hos.4.12-Hos.4.14">Hos 4:12-14</reference>; and Judah admonished to beware of these sins, which would leave her rebellious sister Israel helpless and desolate as a lamb in a desert, <reference osisRef="Hos.4.15">Hos 4:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Hos.4.16">Hos 4:16</reference>. In the remaining verses the style is varied, but the subject is the same. Ephraim is given up to idolatry, and the necessary consequence declared to be a bitter draught! Immediately we see him bound in the wings of a mighty tempest, and driven as chaff before the wind, either to destruction or captivity, <reference osisRef="Hos.4.17-Hos.4.19">Hos 4:17-19</reference>. <div eID="gen33616" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33617" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen33617" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33618" type="x-p"/> The Lord hath a controversy - ריב rib, what we should call a lawsuit, in which God is plaintiff, and the Israelites defendants. It is Jehovah versus Israel and Judah. <div eID="gen33618" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33619" type="x-p"/> But when has God a controversy with any land? - Answer. When there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land. These refer to the minds of the people. But wherever these righteous principles are wanting, there will soon be a vicious practice; hence it is added,
entries.7d77e6d79e1479864791ef7059f05b5f57e812ba: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen33619" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33620" type="x-p"/> By swearing, and lying - Where there is no truth there will be lies and perjury; for false swearing is brought in to confirm lying statements. And when there is no mercy, killing, slaying, and murders, will be frequent. And where there is no knowledge of God, no conviction of his omnipresence and omniscience, private offenses, such as stealing, adulteries, etc., will prevail. These, sooner or later, break out, become a flood, and carry all before them. Private stealing will assume the form of a public robbery, and adulteries become fashionable, especially among the higher orders; and suits of crim. con. render them more public, scandalous, and corrupting. By the examination of witnesses, and reading of infamous letters in a court of justice, people are taught the wiles and stratagems to be used to accomplish these ends, and prevent detection; and also how to avoid those circumstances which have led to the detection of others. Every report of such matters is an experimental lecture on successful debauchery. <div eID="gen33620" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33621" type="x-p"/> Blood toucheth blood - Murders are not only frequent, but assassinations are mutual. Men go out to kill each other; as in our duels, the frenzy of cowards; and as there is no law regarded, and no justice in the land, the nearest akin slays the murderer. Even in our land, where duels are so frequent, if a man kill his antagonist, it is murder; and so generally brought in by an honest coroner and his jury. It is then brought into court; but who is hanged for it? The very murder is considered as an affair of honor, though it began in a dispute about a prostitute; and it is directed to be brought in manslaughter; and the murderer is slightly fined for having hurried his neighbor, perhaps once his friend, into the eternal world, with all his imperfections on his head! No wonder that a land mourns where these prevail; and that God should have a controversy with it. Such crimes as these are sufficient to bring God's curse upon any land. And how does God show his displeasure? See the following verse.
entries.ec4912ec209a489b8896a3084d07d4990cb9bce0: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen33621" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33622" type="x-p"/> Therefore shall the land mourn - Fruitful seasons shall be denied. <div eID="gen33622" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33623" type="x-p"/> That dwelleth therein shall languish - Endemic and epidemic disorders shall prevail, and multitudes shall die; so that mourning shall be found in all quarters. <div eID="gen33623" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33624" type="x-p"/> The beasts of the field, and with the fowls - There is a death of cattle and domestic animals, in consequence of the badness of the season. <div eID="gen33624" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33625" type="x-p"/> The fishes of the sea also shall be taken away - Those immense shoals which at certain seasons frequent the coasts, which are caught in millions, and become a very useful home supply, and a branch of most profitable traffic, they shall be directed by the unseen influence of God to avoid our coasts, as has frequently been the case with herrings, mackerel, pilchards, etc.; and so this source of supply and wealth has been shut up, because of the iniquities of the land.
entries.86204c1c5f9c2d8acd7133d5a4d22eb2fa0b4f5a: <hi type="bold">Verse 4</hi> <div eID="gen33625" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33626" type="x-p"/> Yet let no man strive - Or, no man contendeth. All these evils stalk abroad unreproved, for all are guilty. None can say, "Let me pluck the mote out of thy eye," because he knows that "there is a beam in his own." <div eID="gen33626" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33627" type="x-p"/> For thy people are - The people and the priest are alike rebels against the Lord; the priests having become idolaters, as well as the people. Bp. Newcome renders this clause, "And as is the provocation of the priest, so is that of my people." The whole clause in the original is ועמך כמריבי כהן veammecha kimeribey cohen, "and thy people as the rebellions of the priest." But one of my oldest MSS. omits כהן cohen, "priest;" and then the text may be read, And thy people are as rebels. In this MS. כהן cohen is added in the margin by a much later hand.
entries.64d5a94a41582e04a7a28db79f8fb1e028cea931: <hi type="bold">Verse 5</hi> <div eID="gen33627" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33628" type="x-p"/> Therefore shalt thou fall in the day - In the most open and public manner, without snare or ambush. <div eID="gen33628" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33629" type="x-p"/> And the prophet also shall fall - in the night - The false prophet, when employed in taking prognostications from stars, meteors, etc. <div eID="gen33629" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33630" type="x-p"/> And I will destroy thy mother - The metropolis or mother city. Jerusalem or Samaria is meant.
entries.5d3c251f21f274ec885d6e83f88cc0b6000c7159: <hi type="bold">Verse 6</hi> <div eID="gen33630" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33631" type="x-p"/> My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge - They have not the knowledge of God, nor of sacred things, nor of their own interest, nor of the danger to which they are exposed.
